notes.title: Have You Played Qbeh-1: The Atlas Cube?
notes.content:
Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives. One a day, every day, perhaps for all time…

If Minecraft had been a chilled out puzzle platformer instead of a chilled out survival-esque sandbox, it would probably look a lot like Qbeh-1: The Atlas Cube. Accompanied by the same kind of easy-going, zen-like tunes as its voxel cousin, Qbeh-1 delights in the simple pleasures of collecting a bunch of blocks and using them to create makeshift bridges and steps in order to reach your next goal.

(more…)

notes.title: Level Building Contest
notes.content:
Steam user Mrs Ellie (who previously wrote about leveldesign in Qbeh-1 [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=548624122]here[/url]) has organised a levelbuilding contest! From now until May 7th, everyone in the Qbeh-community is invited to create their own levels and submit them to the contest! The theme is "Ruins", but you may interpret that in whatever way you choose. The 4 winners will each receive a free download code for the [url=https://launchablesocks.bandcamp.com/album/qbeh-1-ost]Qbeh-1 original soundtrack[/url]! 

We can't wait to see what people come up with, so head over to the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/252550/discussions/0/371919771744949597/]forums[/url] for the contest rules and go make some awesome levels!

notes.title: Community Levels
notes.content:
Qbeh-1 level editor is now a bit over one month old. While you can still experience some bugs - and the editor still doesn't have all of the assets you can find in the main game - that hasn't stopped you from creating exciting and interesting levels for others to venture in.

We decided to feature different community levels from time to time. We might even turn this into a monthly thing. What do you guys & girls think?

[img]https://i.imgur.com/bcpVRI7.jpg[/img][h1]Disparity[/h1] by Steam user [b]Don "Newton" Quixote[/b]

First community level we wanted to feature is [i]Disparity[/i] by Steam user [b]Don "Newton" Quixote[/b]. This level has a mysterious feeling with interesting use of both the geometry and lighting in its level design. The creator even hid in some secrets for you to find out! We suggest to check this one out and of course check out what other levels our players have uploaded into the workshop.

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=535340839] Download Disparity here.[/url]

notes.title: Oculus Rift Support is now LIVE!
notes.content:
[img]http://digitaltribegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/Qbeh-1_Rift_Announcement.jpg[/img]

Digital Tribe and Liquid Flower announce that the critically acclaimed [i]QBEH-1: The Atlas Cube[/i] has entered an all new dimension of fun - [b]Oculus Rift support is now live on Steam![/b]

The VR gaming community can finally see for themselves why virtual reality focused journalists are giving [i]QBEH-1: The Atlas Cube[/i] high praise.
 
[i]“Zen-like one moment, vertigo-inducing the next, this is a polished and immersive FPS platformer for the Oculus Rift that's greatly improved by its use of virtual reality.”[/i]
-     [url=http://www.theriftarcade.com/qbeh-1-the-atlas-cube-review/]The Rift Arcade[/url] | [b]8/10[/b]
 
[i]“…this is quite freaking amazing. It really adds a whole level of immersion here.” “It is definitely one of those games I will be going back to play.”[/i]
-     [url=http://youtu.be/X1EL3BJMZFQ]Oculus Rifter[/url]
 
[i]“Qbeh-1 take’s everything that made Portal’s puzzles great and mix’s it with elements of MineCraft and even Tetris and blends them all together to create something unique yet familiar. Its Rift implementation is the best we have seen yet from a previously released 2D game so much so that it’s hard to imagine that it was not originally designed with VR in mind. Qbeh-1 is well worth your time and money as it’s a modern classic and a must play experience.”[/i]
-     [url=http://www.virtualrealityreviewer.com/GAME-detail/qbeh-1-atlas-cube-review/]Virtual Reality Reviewer[/url] | [b]4/5[/b]
 
[h1]QBEH-1 VR FEATURES[/h1]
[list]
   [*]Initially supports Oculus Rift DK1 units with unofficial DK2 support
   [*]Oculus Rift is supported in the Steam Demo
   [*]Game detects Oculus connection and asks if players would like to play it in VR or Regular Mode when launched
   [*]Ability to switch VR on and off at any time in-game
   [*]In-game HUD and menus have been customized for the best VR experience
[/list]

notes.title: Mac version released!
notes.content:
[h1]We are happy to announce that Qbeh-1 has finally found its way to your Steam powered Mac![/h1]

We here at Digital Tribe and Liquid Flower could not let PC gamers have all the fun so are happy to announce that the [b]QBEH-1: The Atlas Cube[/b] Mac version is now available on Steam.

[b]QBEH-1: The Atlas Cube[/b] is an atmospheric 1st-person puzzle platformer that takes players on an inspired quest through a variety of divergent worlds, each filled with new mysteries and secrets to uncover. In each world, players find special cubes that must be collected and used to navigate to the next portal.

Now the Mac gaming community can see why journalists the world over are giving [b]Qbeh-1: The Atlas Cube[/b] scores like 4.5/5, 90/100 and 10/10.

“[i]A simple idea has been taken and turned into a complex puzzle game, with stunning visuals and relaxing music. If you've not played this great indie title yet, I highly suggest you give it a go![/i]”
-	Glacier Gaming | 10/10

“[i]Qbeh-1 is a beautifully crafted atmospheric puzzle adventure that is one of the first "must have" indie titles of the year[/i]”
-	GAMbit Magazine | 4.5/5

“[i]...if you are fans of Zelda’s puzzles, Portal’s genius, and a nice state of zen, there isn’t a better time to jump into this game than now.[/i]”
-	Mod Vive | 90/100

“[i]It’s peaceful, intellectually rewarding, and of all things a stress reliever. Qbeh-1: The Atlas Cube, is great.[/i]”
-	Hooked Gamers | 9/10

It is not just the gaming media that are falling in love with [i]QBEH-1: The Atlas Cube[/i] either! User reviews on Steam are filled with thumbs up “recommended” where players are calling the game “[i]almost magical with the brilliant level and sound design[/i]”, “[i]an awesome labor of love[/i]”, “[i]incredibly beautiful[/i]” and “[i]simply amazing[/i]”.

[b]FEATURES[/b][list]
  [*]Solve elaborate puzzles using a variety of Cube types such as Building Blocks, Energy Cubes and Gravity Manipulators 
  [*]Explore atmospheric Worlds, each with 6 challenging levels and unique themes 
  [*]Discover alternate paths, intriguing platforming elements and secrets to unlock an unfolding mystery 
  [*]Experience an immersive & mesmerizing Soundtrack that pulls you into the adventure 
[/list]
The inspiring [b]QBEH-1: The Atlas Cube[/b] original soundtrack by Launchable Socks, including never before heard bonus tracks, can be found and purchased on Bandcamp: http://launchablesocks.bandcamp.com/album/qbeh-1-ost

notes.title: Update 1.0.1 + Free Soundtrack!
notes.content:
We've just released the first update to Qbeh-1.
You can find the changelog in the forums.

This update also has the official soundtrack bundled with it.
The soundtrack will be available with the game until May 29th 2014.
You can find the soundtrack in the game's folder, which you can access like this, for example:
[list]
[*]Right Click on Qbeh­1: The Atlas Cube in your Library
[*]Select Properties
[*]Click on LOCAL FILES tab
[*]Click on BROWSE LOCAL FILES
[*]Here you will see a folder called “Soundtrack”
[*]Copy & Paste this folder to your Music folder
[*]You now own the Qbeh­1 OST!
[/list]
